description: Corresponding surface landmarks on ICT-FaceKit (generic neutral topology) and Microsoft Rocketbox Female_Adult_01 (facial FBX, as msf_tools.evaluate_geometry orders its vertices), used by rig_gains.py to compare how the two rigs move for the same ARKit shape. Indices are 0-based vertex indices.

conventions.ict: centimetres; y up; faces +z; the face's own left is +x
conventions.rocketbox_female: metres; z up; faces -y; the face's own left is +x
conventions.IOD: distance between the two eyeball centres along the left axis; eyeball centre = mean of the eyeball's vertices
conventions.frontal snap: the front-facing skin vertex (normal . forward > 0.25) nearest to a point in the left/up plane, the most forward one within 0.02 IOD of the nearest distance
conventions.midline profile: skin vertices within 0.03 IOD of the midline that lie within 0.02 IOD of the most forward such vertex within 0.08 IOD above or below them

transfer: Rocketbox brows (Multi-PIE 17, 19, 21, 22, 24, 26) are offsets from the eye-corner midpoint in units of the eye width (corner distance), copied from ICT; alae (31, 35) are offsets from nose_tip and jaw points (6, 10) offsets from chin, in IOD units; each then frontal-snapped on Rocketbox. Rocketbox has no brow geometry, so its brow points are placements, not features.
tooling: Rules were applied with a numpy script outside the repository (msf _viz/k3/pick2.py); the hand picks were made on labelled renders and every landmark was checked on frontal, 3/4 and profile overlays of both rigs. The indices below are the frozen result.
